interest: This file offers a revealing glimpse into U.S. interagency intelligence coordination and counter-intelligence surveillance between the War Department (G-2), ONI, FBI, and the Department of State in the tense year preceding the outbreak of the Pacific War. It documents the movements of Major Ichiji Sugita—a key Japanese military intelligence officer specializing in the United States who would later be present at the British surrender of Singapore in 1942 and the formal Japanese surrender aboard the USS Missouri in 1945—as he embarked on an extensive reconnaissance and liaison tour across the United States and Mexico. The correspondence also demonstrates American concern regarding Japanese military intelligence activities extending into Latin America, showing how State Department diplomatic posts in Mexico were alerted to track visiting Japanese officers.
overview: This file (decimal file 894.2311/1) consists of War Department and Department of State correspondence from late December 1940 and January 1941 concerning the travels of Major Ichiji Sugita, Chief of the American Section of the Japanese Army General Staff, to the United States and Mexico. Transmitted by Brigadier General Sherman Miles of Army Intelligence (G-2) to Assistant Secretary of State Adolf A. Berle, Jr., the intelligence—originally sent via radiogram from Tokyo—reported that Major Sugita departed Japan on December 28, 1940, aboard the SS Nitta Maru for a three-month itinerary covering San Francisco, Los Angeles, Atlanta, Chicago, Washington, and Mexico City. The file traces the dissemination of this intelligence across military corps areas, naval intelligence, the FBI, and onwards from the State Department to the U.S. Embassy in Mexico City, illustrating American surveillance of Japanese military personnel in North America on the eve of the Pacific War.

subfiles.about: Transmittal of three military intelligence reports from the War Department to Assistant Secretary of State A. A. Berle, Jr.
subfiles.from: Brigadier General Sherman Miles, Acting Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, War Department
subfiles.summary: Brigadier General Sherman Miles, Acting Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, forwards three military intelligence enclosures to Assistant Secretary of State Adolf A. Berle, Jr. for information and action. The listed enclosures include a report from the 2nd Corps Area regarding 'The Brotherhood of the Sea', a paraphrase of Radiogram No. 439 from Tokyo concerning Major Sugita, and a summary from the 1st Corps Area regarding Yao Nan Chang. The transmittal letter was received by the Department of State and filed under decimal classification 894.2311/1 by the Division of Protocol.

subfiles.about: Paraphrase of a radiogram from Tokyo reporting the departure and three-month North American itinerary of Major Sugita of the Japanese General Staff.
subfiles.from: U.S. Military Attaché / G-2 Representative, Tokyo, Japan
subfiles.summary: A confidential paraphrase of Radiogram No. 439 sent from Tokyo on December 30, 1940, reports that Major Sugita, Chief of the American Section of the Japanese General Staff, sailed on December 28 aboard the SS Nitta Maru bound for San Francisco. The radiogram notes that he will spend approximately three months in the United States, with an itinerary covering Los Angeles, Atlanta, Chicago, Washington, and Mexico City. It references an earlier pouch letter not yet received and details broad intelligence distribution to the FBI, ONI, State Department, and multiple U.S. Army Corps Areas and the Hawaiian Department.
subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Radiogram No. 439 from Tokyo regarding Major Sugita's departure and itinerary
subfiles.to: Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, War Department

subfiles.about: Diplomatic instruction informing the U.S. Chargé d'Affaires in Mexico City of Major Sugita's arrival and planned visit.
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 3414 from the Department of State informs the American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim in Mexico City of intelligence concerning Major Sugita, Chief of the American Section of the Japanese General Staff. The dispatch recounts that Sugita departed Japan on December 28 aboard the SS Nitta Maru (rendered in the text as SS Hitta Maru) for San Francisco. The Chargé is informed that Sugita plans to spend three months traveling through various American cities and will also visit Mexico City.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 3414 to the American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim in Mexico City regarding Major Sugita
subfiles.to: American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Mexico City, Mexico
